title: Mentoring a Struggling Employee
paragraphs: Rather than recommending that a consistently underperforming employee simply be let go, Farah offered to personally mentor him for one month, believing his struggles came from unclear guidance rather than a lack of ability.
This decision required Farah to spend extra hours after her own workday, time that her manager did not officially recognize or compensate her for during that period.
Within a few weeks, the employee's performance noticeably improved once he understood the expectations clearly, something that had never been properly explained to him during his initial onboarding.
When asked why she invested so much unpaid effort into someone else's success, Farah simply said that giving people a genuine chance mattered more to her than any personal recognition.
